original_value: This paper deals with the issue of the perceptual aspects of selected graphic variables (specifically shape and size) and map background in cartographic visualization. The continued experimental study is based on previous findings and the presupposed cross-cultural universality of shape and size as a graphic variable. The results bring a new perspective on the usage of shape, size and presence/absence of background as graphic variables, as well as a comparison to previous studies. The results suggest that all examined variables influence the speed of processing. Respondents (Czech and Chinese, N = 69) identified target stimuli faster without a map background, with larger stimuli, and with triangular and circular shapes. Czech respondents were universally faster than Chinese respondents. The implications of our research were discussed, and further directions were outlined.

result.paraphrase: This study examines the perceptual aspects of selected graphic variables—namely shape, size, and map background—in cartographic visualization. Building on earlier findings and the presumed cross-cultural universality of shape and size as graphic variables, the ongoing experimental research offers a new perspective on the use of shape, size, and the presence or absence of background, along with a comparison with prior studies. The findings indicate that all investigated variables affect processing speed. Czech and Chinese respondents (N = 69) identified target stimuli more quickly when no map background was present, when the stimuli were larger, and when they were triangular or circular. Czech participants were consistently faster than Chinese participants. The study’s implications were discussed and further research directions were outlined.
